_comment: A world that burns (design 5.2.2). What it *is* is the phenomenon; the rest is what an inferno Age
looks like when the writer said nothing else -- and that sentence is finally true, because the
`requests` block is laid *under* the sentence rather than over it. Write `a blue sun. an inferno Age.`
and you get your blue sun, uncharged; the offer simply is not there to argue with.
Temperature and rainfall are demands rather than limits, and that is the whole difference between
'reached for' and 'insisted on' (Jonah, 2026-08-08). A limit yields silently to anything outside it, so
`frozen inferno` would have been free -- and writing a frozen world that burns is a contradiction a
writer should pay for, exactly as `scorching frozen` already does. A demand fractures against one it
cannot meet, which is the charge. Compatible words still merge: `warm inferno` is not a quarrel.
The embers are required and undrawn. They are the largest warning a player gets, which is why no other
word may offer them (VocabularyCheck holds it) -- and a signal that only fires two Ages in three is no
better than one that fires where nothing is burning. They were pooled until 2026-09-01 and should not
be again.
**The sky is where an inferno differs from mere heat.** `scorching` is a hot climate and leans on the
ground; this is the air itself alight, so it asks for a sky to match and asks harder: two or three suns
where scorching asks at most a second, red *or blue* where scorching keeps to the warm end -- a blue
star burns hotter than a red one, and that is the point of it -- and three facets drawn where scorching
draws one. `sun.cast` is the only way a word can bring a body into being: a writer mints a sun by
describing one, and there is no clause in `an inferno Age` to mint anything.
**The sea is offered rather than set, and by tag rather than by parameter**, because a sea is a value from
a catalogue and there is no parameter that says `lava`. The tilt is the one kind of claim that yields by
construction: it leans the draw between whatever survived, so `an inferno Age. A drowned sea.` leaves
water the only survivor and the lean is simply spent on it. Lava first, air close behind -- a world
that burns has either a sea of fire or none at all -- and water pushed away, which is what stops the
readiness of the ordinary answer carrying the day in a world where it has no business.
Every parameter here names its aspect. Unqualified they would reach every aspect owning the name, so
`colour` would paint the grass and the leaves and `size` would quietly shrink the trees.
Instability never compounds through this. A manifestation is bought with the index after the index is
settled, so only what is *written* can charge -- an inferno the Art inflicted on a broken Age cannot
make it more broken.
